title: Sprint interop deploy lane and cadence experiments - 2wk notes
body:
Purpose:
Run a lightweight two-week experiment that treats the sprint deploy as an interoperable lane: low-friction, measurable canaries, and rapid rollback windows. Capture ops playbook, a compact calendar, and a release-notes sketch to test whether shifting from big-bang weekends -> many small interop lanes reduces post-release noise and mean time to detect.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Goal: cut median incident MTTD by 30% and decrease change-set blast radius via smaller, frequent deploy lanes.
- Experiment window: 2026-12-06 -> 2026-12-19 (two sprints-ish).
- Deploy frequency target: 3 small lanes per week (mon/wed/fri mornings, staggered by team).
- Success metrics: MTTD, rollback rate, customer error rate (5xx), median end-to-end latency 95th percentile, deploy pain hours.

Runbook checklist (compact):
- Preflight (T-48h):
  - Create deploy ticket and tag with lane-id (LANE-2026-12-A/B/C).
  - Confirm health dashboard deck update (route-level latency, error rates, token-cost spikes).
  - Attach smoke scripts in PR (smoke: /ops/smoke/interop-basic.sh).
  - Slack announce to #deploy-lane-ops with planned windows and canary percentages.
  - Verify required migrations are backwards compatible; if not, schedule DB window.
  - Notify SRE and owning service pager-duty rotation.
- T-2h:
  - Run quick dry-run locally: smoke script against staging.
  - Ensure canary config is in feature-flags repo and set to default hold.
  - Collect golden traces for main routes for comparison (trace ids pinned in ticket).
- Deploy (T+0):
  - Kick off lane deploy via CI pipeline (GH action: lane-deploy).
  - Start with first canary wave: 1% of traffic for 10 minutes.
  - Run smoke checks (end-to-end happy path, embeddings regression quick check, KV cache warm-up).
  - Telemetry gates: no >2x error spike vs baseline, no latency regression >20% p95, no token-cost jump >15%.
  - Escalation: if any gate trips, abort and run rollback-quick.
- Gradual expansion:
  - 1% -> 5% after 20m (if gates pass).
  - 5% -> 20% after 30m.
  - 20% -> 50% after 45m.
  - Full 100% if stable for 60m at 50%.
- Post-deploy (T+4h & T+24h):
  - Run validation suite for customer-critical prompts (prompt set stored in /evals/lane-interop/seedset.json).
  - Mark rollout notes in ticket and tick off smoke checklist.
  - Capture anomalous traces into deploy ticket for later blameless postmortem if needed.

Canary and rollback matrix (quick):
- Gate conditions that force rollback:
  - Any sustained new 5xx class errors exceeding baseline+5 for >5 minutes.
  - Latency p95 regression >30% for >10 minutes on primary routes.
  - Model output quality regression flagged by run-of-eval (semantic drift > threshold).
  - Cost-per-token increase >25% unexplained by config.
- Rollback steps:
  1) Trigger pipeline rollback action (GH action: lane-rollback) from ticket.
  2) Change feature-flag to previous stable commit (FF manager).
  3) Notify SRE and product: immediate update to #deploy-lane-ops and affected product slack.
  4) Open post-rollback incident stub with runbook fields filled.

Compact calendar (week matrix for experiment window):
- Week 1 (2026-12-06 -> 2026-12-12):
  - Mon 08:30: LANE-A (model routing change, small config): 1% -> 50% over 1.5h.
  - Wed 09:00: LANE-B (dedicated autoscaler tweak): 1% -> 20% -> monitor overnight.
  - Fri 08:30: LANE-C (observability instrumentation + sampling change): 1% -> 100% quick ramp after 2h.
- Week 2 (2026-12-13 -> 2026-12-19):
  - Mon 08:30: LANE-D (canary variant: quantization profile swap for batch jobs): limited to non-critical regions.
  - Wed 09:00: LANE-E (rollout rollback drill + safety-lane): purpose-built for practicing rollback).
  - Fri 08:30: LANE-F (open slot: catch-up or emergency patch).

Housekeeping and telemetry expectations:
- Dashboard panels to watch live: route-p95, route-mean, 5xx-rate, embedding-distance-distribution, token-cost-per-req.
- Tracing: sample at 10% for these lanes; increase to 50% on any anomaly.
- Logs: add lane-id tag to all service logs for filtering.
- Alerting: temporary lowered thresholds for experiment lanes (sensitivity up for MTTD measurement).

Release notes draft (for internal channel and quick customer-facing blurb):
- Internal release-note snippet (short):
  "Sprint Interop lanes: this week we launched a set of small-batch deployment lanes to validate faster, low-risk rollouts. Changes include an autoscaler tuning for the Dedicated path, a model quantization trial in a limited region, and improved sampling for tracing. If you see anomalies on /v1/generate or embedding endpoints, please ping #deploy-lane-ops and include lane-id."
- Customer-facing blurb (short, conservative):
  "Maintenance window: minor performance improvements and telemetry enhancements were rolled out incrementally across small traffic lanes this week to improve latency stability. No customer action required; contact support if you notice degraded inference latency or quality."
- Detailed release notes section (for ticket closure):
  - LANE-A: route routing tweak; config diff: config/routes.yaml @ commit abc123 -> def456; expected impact: marginal routing efficiency +1–3% p50.
  - LANE-B: autoscaler target adjustment for model-worker pool (min=2 -> min=3 in region eu-west).
  - LANE-C: tracing sampling change: default sample rate increased from 1% -> 10% for critical endpoints.
  - LANE-D: quantization profile Q4_8 trial in ap-northeast (limited weight set).

Observability checks (post-deploy quick list):
- Verify no new alert flood in last 2h.
- Confirm trace error spikes correlate with deploy window or are pre-existing.
- Validate embedding cosine distribution did not shift by >3 SD.
- Manual prompt-set: run 10 golden prompts, compare tokens and responses; log diffs to ticket.

Open questions / notes-to-self (fragments):
- How much of the increased MTTD sensitivity is due to lowered alert thresholds vs real regressions? Track both.
- Need a small harness that auto-samples a set of representative prompts and runs inference against both old and new variants during canary waves. Reduce manual checks.
- Consider defaulting post-deploy telemetry retention for lanes to 72h to help debug transient regressions.
- If we see model-quality drift in LANE-D, run immediate A/B eval with seed prompts and push findings to product for rollback decision.

Experiment wrap & data capture (what to log):
- For each lane: timestamped snapshot of gate metrics, canary wave sizes, commit id, infra allocation (GPU type + count), feature-flag state, and golden-trace ids.
- Link to ticket naming convention: DEPLOY-LANE-<lane-id>-<YYYYMMDD>. Example: DEPLOY-LANE-A-20261206.

Communication templates (short):
- Slack alert (on canary fail):
  "[LANE-A] Canary gate failed at T+14m: route /v1/generate p95 +38% vs baseline. Rolling back now. Ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/PLAT-7842"
- Post-deploy summary (auto-post to #deploy-lane-ops):
  "LANE-B completed: 3h stable at 50% -> promoting to 100%. No gating events. Keys: commit def456, infra: g5-16x. If you hit issues, mention DEPLOY-LANE-B-20261208."

A/B: rollback drill (Wed):
- Purpose: validate rollback plumbing under realistic pressure.
- Steps: deploy a harmless config change (feature flag for telemetry naming), then intentionally flip the model-variant flag to a canary that triggers a synthetic latency increase. Trigger alert and execute rollback; record true-to-run time to rollback.

Post-mortem blameless template (if failure occurs):
- Summary: short description of what happened.
- Timeline: T-48h -> T+72h with timestamps.
- Contributing factors: list.
- Mitigations taken.
- Follow-ups: owners and target dates.

Metrics to collect during experiment (by priority):
1) MTTD (median + 90th).
2) Rollback rate per deploy.
3) Customer-facing error rate (5xx) delta.
4) p95 latency delta on primary routes.
5) Operator hours spent on deploys per week.
6) Model quality drift score via eval harness.

Links / pointers (working):
- CI deploy action: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/actions/workflows/lane-deploy.yml
- Smoke scripts: /ops/smoke/interop-basic.sh (repo: infra-ops)
- Eval seedset: https://evals.redwood.ai/sets/interop-seedset-v1.json
- Jira epic: PLAT-7842 (experiment tracking).

Next steps (immediate):
- Finalize smoke harness automation (owner: Marcus Lee, due: 2026-12-08).
- Wire lane-id into log enrichment pipeline (owner: Daniel Cho, due: 2026-12-10).
- Run rollback drill (LANE-E) on 2026-12-15, gather timing metrics.
- Post-experiment review on 2026-12-20: bring data (MTTD, rollback rate, operator hours) and decide whether to adopt lane cadence.

Notes-to-self end: keep the lanes small, own the signal_collection, and avoid big infra moves in this experiment window. This doc will be the canonical lightweight guide for the two-week interop lane experiment.
